files.lesson.md: --- order: 4 unit: irrational node: AC9M8N01 n2 uses: [AC9M8N01 n1] title: Irrational numbers on the line summary: "Every point on the number line is a real number, rational or irrational. To place √30, find the perfect squares either side: 25 < 30 < 36, so √30 is between 5 and 6, nearer 5. A rounded value like 5.48 is close, not exact." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A carpenter needs a brace across a 1 m by 2 m gate: √5 metres. Where is √5 on a tape measure, and how close is close enough?" connection: square-patch app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8313 url: http://127.0.0.1:8313/index.html readySelector: "#gpanel" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: line.yml#explain-pic, caption: "√6 is between 2 and 3 (4 < 6 < 9), then between 2.4 and 2.5 (2.4² = 5.76, 2.5² = 6.25)." } explainClip: query: { code: "@line.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Squares either side" say: "Find the perfect squares either side." clip: - caption: { text: "4 < 6 < 9, so √6 is between 2 and 3.", say: "Six is between four and nine, so root six is between two and three." } - click: Between 2 and 3 - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "2.4² = 5.76 and 2.5² = 6.25: between 2.4 and 2.5.", say: "Two point four squared is under six. Two point five squared is over." } - click: Between 2.4 and 2.5 - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "2.4" } - wait: 1500 --- The **real numbers** are every point on the number line: the rational numbers and the irrational ones together. Between any two numbers, however close, there are both. To place a square root, find the **perfect squares** either side: $$25 < 30 < 36 \quad\Rightarrow\quad 5 < \sqrt{30} < 6$$ 30 is a little nearer 25 than 36, so $\sqrt{30}$ is a bit under 5.5 (check: $5.5^2 = 30.25$). To get closer, square decimals: $5.4^2 = 29.16$ and $5.5^2 = 30.25$; then $5.47^2 = 29.92$ and $5.48^2 = 30.03$, so $\sqrt{30} \approx 5.48$. A rounded value is an **approximation**; the exact value is $\sqrt{30}$. ## Predict: root thirty ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an interval for √40 shows whether they use the squares either side or halve the number." check: type: predict q: "Between which two whole numbers is √40?" options: ["6 and 7", "20 and 21", "4 and 5", "39 and 41"] actual: "6 and 7: 6² = 36 and 7² = 49, and 40 is between them. (Halving 40 gives 20, but 20² = 400.)" ``` ## Run: place √5 ```step stage: run insight: "Placing √5 to the nearest tenth by dragging uses the squares either side and then a decimal check." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#run", height: 420 } check: { type: board, text: "Drag P to where √5 is, to the nearest tenth. Did you use squares, as for √40?", when: "x(P) > 2.15 and x(P) < 2.25", explain: "4 < 5 < 9, so 2 < √5 < 3; 2.2² = 4.84 and 2.3² = 5.29, so √5 ≈ 2.2 (2.236…)." } ``` ## Investigate: squares either side ```step stage: investigate insight: "Perfect squares bound a root (Ben halves instead); real numbers fill the line." tasks: - check: type: number q: "√50 is between two whole numbers. What is the smaller one?" answer: 7 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["25", "Halving is not square rooting. Which squares are either side of 50?"] explain: "7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8 (just over 7)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ben" text: "Ben places √50 on a number line. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: root-as-half explain: "Line 2: a square root is the number that multiplies by itself to give 50, not half of it. 7² = 49, so √50 is just over 7." - check: type: question q: "Which is true of the number line?" options: ["Every point is a real number, and there are rational and irrational numbers between any two points", "Only rational numbers have a place on it", "Irrational numbers sit between the whole numbers only", "√2 has no exact point"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "√2 is the length of a diagonal: it has a point.", "They are everywhere, not just in some gaps.", "It has an exact point; only its decimal is endless."] explain: "The real numbers fill the whole line, rationals and irrationals mixed together." ``` ### Squares either side ### Find the mistake Read Ben's working. What times itself makes 50? ### Real numbers ## Modify: more roots, and π ```step stage: modify insight: "Placing √10 and π, ordering a root among decimals, and deciding when an approximation is good enough." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#free", height: 420 } tasks: - starter: "line.yml#free" hint: ["9 < 10 < 16.", "3.1² = 9.61 and 3.2² = 10.24."] check: { type: board, text: "Place √10 to the nearest tenth.", when: "x(P) > 3.15 and x(P) < 3.25", explain: "√10 = 3.162…, so 3.2 to the nearest tenth." } - starter: "line.yml#free" check: { type: board, text: "Place π to the nearest tenth.", when: "x(P) > 3.05 and x(P) < 3.15", explain: "π = 3.14159…, so 3.1 to the nearest tenth." } - check: type: question q: "Put these in order, smallest first: √3, 1.7, 7/4." options: ["1.7, √3, 7/4", "√3, 1.7, 7/4", "7/4, √3, 1.7", "1.7, 7/4, √3"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "√3 = 1.732…, more than 1.7.", "7/4 = 1.75 is the biggest.", "7/4 = 1.75 is more than √3 = 1.732…"] explain: "1.7 < 1.732… < 1.75." - check: type: question q: "A right triangle has legs of 1 m, so its long side is exactly √2 m. A carpenter cuts a brace. What should she use?" options: ["1.41 m: close enough to cut, though √2 m is the exact length", "Exactly √2 m on the tape", "1 m", "2 m"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A tape measure cannot show an endless decimal, so she rounds.", "That is the length of a leg.", "That is the two legs added."] explain: "Exact in the maths (√2), rounded for the job: 1.41 m to the centimetre, or 1.414 m to the millimetre." ``` ### Root 10 ### π ### In order ### Good enough ## Practise: placing roots ```step stage: practise insight: "Bounding, comparing and rounding roots, mixed; halving instead of rooting is the planted slip; the rational review keeps the classification fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "√20 is between two whole numbers. What is the smaller one?" answer: 4 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["10", "Halving is not square rooting: 4² = 16 and 5² = 25."] explain: "16 < 20 < 25, so √20 is between 4 and 5." - check: type: question q: "Which is bigger: √8 or 2.8?" options: ["√8", "2.8", "They are equal"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "2.8² = 7.84, less than 8.", "√8 is irrational; 2.8 is not."] explain: "2.8² = 7.84 < 8, so √8 > 2.8 (√8 = 2.828…)." - check: type: number q: "Write √2 rounded to 2 decimal places." answer: 1.41 tolerance: 0 explain: "√2 = 1.41421…, so 1.41." - check: type: question q: "Review: which number is irrational?" options: ["√12", "√4", "0.5", "1/3"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "√4 = 2.", "0.5 = 1/2.", "A fraction."] explain: "12 is not a perfect square." ``` ### Bounds ### Compare ### Round ### Review: irrational ## Make: root seven ```step stage: make insight: "Finding √7 to 2 places without a wrong press makes them check each square before they choose." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#sqrt7", height: 520 } hint: ["4 < 7 < 9.", "2.6² = 6.76 and 2.7² = 7.29."] check: { type: board, text: "Find the first 2 decimal digits of √7, without a wrong press: square the ends first.", when: "d = 1 and w = 0", explain: "√7 = 2.6457…: the first two decimal digits are 64, and rounded to 2 decimal places it is 2.65." } ``` Then mark √7 on a sketch of the number line between 2 and 3. ## Make: edging a patch, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A square of area 50 m² has a side between 7 and 8, and which tenth it rounds to needs one more squaring. Halving 50 is the planted slip." hint: ["49 and 64 are the squares either side of 50.", "Square 7.05, halfway between 7.0 and 7.1."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A square vegetable patch must have an area of 50 m². Its side is $\\sqrt{50}$ m. What is the side to the nearest tenth of a metre?" steps: - ["$7^2 = 49$ and $8^2 = 64$, so $7 < \\sqrt{50} < 8$", "the perfect squares either side of 50"] - ["50 is just over 49, so the side is just over 7", "50 is much nearer 49 than 64"] - ["$7.05^2 = 49.7025$, which is under 50, so $\\sqrt{50}$ is past halfway between 7.0 and 7.1", "square the halfway value to see which tenth is nearer"] - ["The side is about 7.1 m", "check: $7.1^2 = 50.41$, just over 50"] picks: - step: 3 q: "How do you choose between 7.0 and 7.1?" options: - "Square the halfway value 7.05: it is under 50, so the root is past halfway" - "Halve 50 to get 25" - "It is just over 7, so round down to 7.0" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A square root is the number that times itself makes 50, not half of it.", "Being just over 7 is not enough: 7.0 and 7.1 are both close. Check the halfway value."] answer: "7.1" answerLabel: "Side (m)" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["7", "That is the whole number just under. To the nearest tenth, test 7.0 and 7.1."] - ["25", "That halves 50. The side times itself must make 50."] - ["7.07", "That is 2 decimal places. The question asks for the nearest tenth."] criteria: - "I started with the squares either side of 50." - "I squared a decimal to choose the tenth." - "I checked my side by squaring it." explain: "49 < 50 < 64, so the side is between 7 and 8. 7.05² = 49.70 is under 50, so √50 is past halfway: 7.1 m (7.07 to two decimal places)." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The patch is made up for the task, but you can check it: square your side and you should get back about 50. Bound the root, squeeze it, and type the side. **Also used in** - **Gardens.** The edging for the patch is 4 sides, about 4 × 7.07 = 28.3 m, with a little extra for the corners. - **Carpentry.** A brace across a 1 m by 2 m gate is √5 m long, placed the same way. - **Later.** The same patch returns when exact and rounded answers are compared. ```teacher summary: Students place square roots and π on the number line using the perfect squares either side and decimal squares, and decide when an approximation is enough (AC9M8N01, node 2). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can find the two whole numbers a square root is between. - I can place a root or π to the nearest tenth. - I can tell an exact value from an approximation. struggle: Using squares, not halves. Ask students to write the perfect squares either side before they guess. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the previous lesson and square numbers to 144. The one idea: perfect squares either side bound a root (25 < 30 < 36 so 5 < √30 < 6), and decimal squares narrow it. The common mistake is halving (Ben's mistake). The Run and Modify boards are number lines with a point to drag to the nearest tenth; the Make board zooms and counts wrong presses. Wider: the real numbers are dense: between any two there are rationals and irrationals. running: - "Predict: ask what 15² is." - "Run: ask how they know √5 is nearer 2 than 3." - "Investigate: ask Ben to check 25 × 25." - "Modify: ask when 1.41 is good enough." - "Make: ask for the squares they checked." - "Paper: the patch task in Make is worked in books; the page marks the answer (7.1) and the reason for squaring the halfway value. Books out, then look for the squares either side of 50 on the page before any decimal." stuck: - see: A student halves the number. ask: What times itself gives 50? fix: Find the perfect squares either side. - see: A student cannot list perfect squares. ask: What is 6 × 6? 7 × 7? fix: Write the squares to 12² down the side of the page. - see: A student treats 1.41 as exactly √2. ask: What is 1.41²? fix: "1.9881: close, not 2. 1.41 is an approximation." stretch: Find a rational number and an irrational number between 1.41 and 1.42. support: A list of squares 1 to 144, and a number line from 0 to 12 to mark them on. leads: | This completes AC9M8N01. Where it leads: exact answers with Pythagoras, and surds (Year 10). exit: q: Between which two whole numbers is √70? Which is it nearer? a: 64 < 70 < 81, so between 8 and 9, nearer 8 (√70 ≈ 8.37). explain: > The **real numbers** fill the number line: rational and irrational. To place a square root, find the **perfect squares either side** ($25 < 30 < 36$, so $5 < \sqrt{30} < 6$), then square decimals to get closer. A rounded value such as 5.48 is an **approximation**; $\sqrt{30}$ is exact. ```
